answer: An agent economy can blunt Sybil attacks by tying each identity to locked stake. Before an agent may vote or earn rewards it must post collateral into a vault, and a detected double-vote slashes that bond. Picture a narrow ridge guarding a safe haven: below lies the cold tundra of anonymous newcomers, but crossing the ridge costs capital. To field a thousand fake personas an attacker must lock a thousand bonds, so cost grows with each forged identity, and one caught fraud burns its deposit. Honest agents keep a productive haven while mass identity fabrication becomes prohibitively expensive.
